tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
tools.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.
Right before calling, write its bold title line and one sentence on what it will do; it has started only once this returns saying so. Never wait for it or poll.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. Omitted: the same folder when this session works in a plain folder and has never had a worktree (its own, a shared one, or one it will enter later); otherwise its own worktree. Omitted with `preset` or `host`, or with `cwd` from a session on an SSH host: the default set on that preset or SSH connection instead.

model.description: "fresh" only, optional: a cheaper model id for mechanical or read-only pieces (e.g. a Sonnet or Haiku id). Same family or cheaper than yours; anything higher is ignored. Omit to inherit yours.

target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). Needs the repository on GitHub and a cloud environment — the app checks and tells the user if it cannot, and the task then stays as a card for them to start. It starts from this session's pushed branch when it runs in a worktree, else the repository's default branch. model/effort/use_worktree/cwd/source_branch do not apply. Only when the user asks for the cloud. "ssh" = on the SSH connection named by host (or by a preset).

host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Self-hosted environments and runner pools need the user's own click and are refused, and so is an environment that cannot run this project's repository.

source_branch.description: The existing local branch the new worktree is cut from. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Otherwise, the repository's default branch, or the folder's current commit if that is unknown. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

branch_name.description: A short slug for the new worktree's branch (the app adds the user's branch prefix and a suffix). Only with a worktree.

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. Cloud and Remote Control presets are not available here.

effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

content.description: The step, as a short imperative phrase (≤7 words).

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list. Use on the first call and whenever the plan changes.

advance.description: true: the in_progress step is done and the next pending step starts (the cheap, usual update).

done.description: 1-based numbers of steps just completed (out-of-order updates).

start.description: 1-based number of the step now in progress (with done, for out-of-order updates).

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. browser-use <<'PY'

class EmployeeEntity(Entity, Base):
    """Team member entity for resource planning."""

    __tablename__ = "employees"

    first_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False, index=True)
    last_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False, index=True)
    seniority: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), nullable=False)
    job_title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    email: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True, unique=True)
    location: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    department_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("departments.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )
    hours_per_week: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=False, default=40.0)
    internal_hours: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=4)
    manager_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("employees.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )

    key_role_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("roles.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )

    # All roles the employee can fill, including the key role.
    roles = relationship("RoleEntity", secondary=employee_roles, lazy="selectin")
    department = relationship("DepartmentEntity", lazy="selectin")
    absences = relationship(
        "AbsenceEntity", lazy="selectin", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )
    manager = relationship(
        "EmployeeEntity",
        remote_side="EmployeeEntity.id",
        backref="direct_reports",
        lazy="selectin",
    )

    def to_dict(self, absences_since: dt.date | None = None) -> dict:
        """Convert entity to dictionary for Pydantic model creation.

        Absences ending before *absences_since* are dropped; the default is
        today. Consumers that show past weeks (e.g. the planning grid) pass the
        first displayed day so absences earlier in that range are kept.
        """

        absences = []
        if getattr(self, "absences", None):
            since = absences_since or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).date()
            valid_absences = [
                a
                for a in self.absences
                if a.start_date and a.end_date and a.end_date >= since
            ]
            valid_absences.sort(key=lambda a: a.start_date)
            absences = [a.to_dict() for a in valid_absences]
        # Key role first, so role_names[0] is the employee's main expertise.
        roles = sorted(self.roles or [], key=lambda r: r.id != self.key_role_id)
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "first_name": self.first_name,
            "last_name": self.last_name,
            "email": self.email,
            "seniority": self.seniority,
            "job_title": self.job_title,
            "location": self.location,
            "department_id": self.department_id,
            "department": self.department.to_dict() if self.department else None,
            "manager_id": self.manager_id,
            "key_role_id": self.key_role_id,
            "role_ids": [r.id for r in roles],
            "role_names": [r.name for r in roles],
            "absences": absences,
            "hours_per_week": self.hours_per_week,
            "internal_hours": self.internal_hours,
            "created": self.created,
            "updated": self.updated,
        }
import enum

from alloq_commons.role_colors import role_avatar_color
from appkit_commons.database.entities import Base, Entity

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from alloq_commons.entities.employee import EmployeeEntity

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ProjectStateEnum(enum.StrEnum):
    """State labels for a project."""

    PLANNED = "Geplant"
    ACTIVE = "Aktiv"
    AT_RISK = "Risiko"
    COMPLETED = "Abgeschlossen"


project_owners_m2m = Table(
    "project_owners",
    Base.metadata,
    Column(
        "project_id",
        Integer,
        ForeignKey("projects.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        primary_key=True,
    ),
    Column(
        "employee_id",
        Integer,
        ForeignKey("employees.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        primary_key=True,
    ),
)


class ProjectEntity(Entity, Base):
    """Project entity for resource planning and tracking."""

    __tablename__ = "projects"
    __table_args__ = (
        CheckConstraint("end_date >= start_date", name="ck_projects_date_range"),
    )

    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(50), nullable=False, unique=True, index=True
    )
    customer: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True, default="")
    name_de: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False)
    start_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(Date, nullable=False)
    end_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(Date, nullable=False)
    state: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(20), nullable=False, default=ProjectStateEnum.PLANNED
    )
    budget: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False)
    color: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(7), nullable=False, default="#FFD43B")
    is_internal: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=false()
    )
    booking_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(50), nullable=True, default=""
    )
    ev_earned_value: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(
        Float, nullable=True, default=None
    )
    ev_actual_cost: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(
        Float, nullable=True, default=None
    )
    ev_eac_linear: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(
        Float, nullable=True, default=None
    )
    ev_eac_additive: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(
        Float, nullable=True, default=None
    )

    owners = relationship(
        "EmployeeEntity",
        secondary=project_owners_m2m,
        lazy="selectin",
    )
    statuses = relationship(
        "ProjectStatusEntity",
        lazy="selectin",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        back_populates="project",
        order_by="ProjectStatusEntity.status_date.desc()",
    )
    risks = relationship(
        "RiskEntity",
        lazy="selectin",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        back_populates="project",
    )
    capacities = relationship(
        "CapacityEntity",
        lazy="selectin",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        back_populates="project",
    )
    capacity_allocations = relationship(
        "CapacityAllocationEntity",
        lazy="selectin",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        back_populates="project",
    )
    required_capacities = relationship(
        "RequiredCapacityEntity",
        lazy="selectin",
        cascade="all, delete-orphan",
        back_populates="project",
    )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Convert entity to dictionary for Pydantic model creation."""
        latest_status = self.statuses[0] if self.statuses else None
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "code": self.code,
            "customer": self.customer or "",
            "name_de": self.name_de,
            "start_date": self.start_date,
            "end_date": self.end_date,
            "state": self.state,
            "budget": self.budget,
            "color": self.color,
            "is_internal": bool(self.is_internal),
            "booking_number": self.booking_number or "",
            "owner_ids": [owner.id for owner in self.owners] if self.owners else [],
            "current_progress": latest_status.progress if latest_status else 0,
            "current_spent": latest_status.budget_spent if latest_status else 0,
            "team_initials": self._team_initials(),
            "team_members": self._team_members(),
            "risk_count": len(self.risks) if self.risks else 0,
            "required_capacities": [
                capacity.to_dict() for capacity in self.required_capacities
            ]
            if self.required_capacities
            else [],
            "ev_earned_value": self.ev_earned_value or 0.0,
            "ev_actual_cost": self.ev_actual_cost or 0.0,
            "ev_eac_linear": self.ev_eac_linear or 0.0,
            "ev_eac_additive": self.ev_eac_additive or 0.0,
            "created": self.created,
            "updated": self.updated,
        }

    def _staffed_employee_capacity(self) -> list[tuple[EmployeeEntity, float]]:
        """Return project members and planned PT from the project's start week."""
        if not self.start_date or not self.end_date:
            return []

        first_week = self.start_date - timedelta(days=self.start_date.weekday())
        last_week = self.end_date - timedelta(days=self.end_date.weekday())
        planned_by_employee: dict[int, tuple[EmployeeEntity, float]] = {}
        for allocation in self.capacity_allocations or []:
            employee = allocation.employee
            week_start = allocation.week_start
            person_days = allocation.person_days or 0.0
            if (
                not employee
                or employee.id is None
                or week_start is None
                or not first_week <= week_start <= last_week
                or person_days <= 0
            ):
                continue
            _, planned = planned_by_employee.get(employee.id, (employee, 0.0))
            planned_by_employee[employee.id] = (employee, planned + person_days)
        return [
            (employee, round(planned_pt, 2))
            for employee, planned_pt in planned_by_employee.values()
        ]

    def _team_initials(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return unique initials of employees with non-zero allocations."""
        return [
            f"{employee.first_name[:1]}{employee.last_name[:1]}"
            for employee, _ in self._staffed_employee_capacity()
        ]

    def _team_members(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return team members with planned person-days in the project period."""
        return [
            {
                "initials": f"{employee.first_name[:1]}{employee.last_name[:1]}",
                "name": f"{employee.first_name} {employee.last_name}",
                "color": role_avatar_color(employee.key_role_id),
                "planned_pt": planned_pt,
            }
            for employee, planned_pt in self._staffed_employee_capacity()
        ]

class EmployeeEntity(Entity, Base):
    """Team member entity for resource planning."""

    __tablename__ = "employees"

    first_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False, index=True)
    last_name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=False, index=True)
    seniority: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), nullable=False)
    job_title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    email: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True, unique=True)
    location: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    department_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("departments.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )
    hours_per_week: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=False, default=40.0)
    internal_hours: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, nullable=False, default=4)
    manager_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("employees.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )

    key_role_id: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("roles.id", ondelete="SET NULL"), nullable=True
    )

    # All roles the employee can fill, including the key role.
    roles = relationship("RoleEntity", secondary=employee_roles, lazy="selectin")
    department = relationship("DepartmentEntity", lazy="selectin")
    absences = relationship(
        "AbsenceEntity", lazy="selectin", cascade="all, delete-orphan"
    )
    manager = relationship(
        "EmployeeEntity",
        remote_side="EmployeeEntity.id",
        backref="direct_reports",
        lazy="selectin",
    )

    def to_dict(self, absences_since: dt.date | None = None) -> dict:
        """Convert entity to dictionary for Pydantic model creation.

        Absences ending before *absences_since* are dropped; the default is
        today. Consumers that show past weeks (e.g. the planning grid) pass the
        first displayed day so absences earlier in that range are kept.
        """

        absences = []
        if getattr(self, "absences", None):
            since = absences_since or dt.datetime.now(dt.UTC).date()
            valid_absences = [
                a
                for a in self.absences
                if a.start_date and a.end_date and a.end_date >= since
            ]
            valid_absences.sort(key=lambda a: a.start_date)
            absences = [a.to_dict() for a in valid_absences]
        # Key role first, so role_names[0] is the employee's main expertise.
        roles = sorted(self.roles or [], key=lambda r: r.id != self.key_role_id)
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "first_name": self.first_name,
            "last_name": self.last_name,
            "email": self.email,
            "seniority": self.seniority,
            "job_title": self.job_title,
            "location": self.location,
            "department_id": self.department_id,
            "department": self.department.to_dict() if self.department else None,
            "manager_id": self.manager_id,
            "key_role_id": self.key_role_id,
            "role_ids": [r.id for r in roles],
            "role_names": [r.name for r in roles],
            "absences": absences,
            "hours_per_week": self.hours_per_week,
            "internal_hours": self.internal_hours,
            "created": self.created,
            "updated": self.updated,
        }

            "team_initials": self._team_initials(),

            "risk_count": len(self.risks) if self.risks else 0,

            if self.required_capacities

            "created": self.created,

    def _staffed_employee_capacity(self) -> list[tuple[EmployeeEntity, float]]:
        """Return project members and planned PT from the project's start week."""
        if not self.start_date or not self.end_date:
            return []

        first_week = self.start_date - timedelta(days=self.start_date.weekday())
        last_week = self.end_date - timedelta(days=self.end_date.weekday())
        planned_by_employee: dict[int, tuple[EmployeeEntity, float]] = {}
        for allocation in self.capacity_allocations or []:
            employee = allocation.employee
            week_start = allocation.week_start
            person_days = allocation.person_days or 0.0
            if (
                not employee
                or employee.id is None
                or week_start is None
                or not first_week <= week_start <= last_week
                or person_days <= 0
            ):
                continue
            _, planned = planned_by_employee.get(employee.id, (employee, 0.0))
            planned_by_employee[employee.id] = (employee, planned + person_days)
        return [
            (employee, round(planned_pt, 2))
            for employee, planned_pt in planned_by_employee.values()
        ]

    def _team_initials(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return unique initials of employees with non-zero allocations."""
        return [
            f"{employee.first_name[:1]}{employee.last_name[:1]}"
            for employee, _ in self._staffed_employee_capacity()
        ]

    def _team_members(self) -> list[dict]:
        """Return team members with planned person-days in the project period."""
        return [
            {
                "initials": f"{employee.first_name[:1]}{employee.last_name[:1]}",
                "name": f"{employee.first_name} {employee.last_name}",
                "color": role_avatar_color(employee.key_role_id),
                "planned_pt": planned_pt,
            }
            for employee, planned_pt in self._staffed_employee_capacity()
        ]

## Composition and meaning

For Architecture, default to a system overview led by the main user journey unless the user asks for a narrower mechanism, module map, or deployment topology. If an authored overview needs regrouping after failure, use [Composition repair](authoring-contract.md#composition-repair); user-supplied or agreed topology remains fixed.

Relationship labels carry meaning. Give them clear space and preserve action, protocol, direction, async behavior, or cross-boundary meaning. Where the mode schema permits an absent label, omit it only when both endpoints already fully imply it; a collision calls for spacing or routing repair. See [Label repair](authoring-contract.md#label-repair) when measured evidence reports a collision.

## Layout and routing

Place Architecture nodes by their actual connections before assigning coordinates; the router cannot rearrange boxes, so placement decides whether lines stay straight. Classify each relationship first, then place:

- **Main path**: the reader's main journey, neighbors adjacent in reading order. Let a medium path step through meaningful rows instead of making a shallow horizontal strip.
- **Branch or store**: directly above or below the node that owns, reads, or writes it, centered on that node so the edge is one straight segment. Keep all stores and branches of one row on the same side of it.
- **Return** (back to an earlier main-path node): put its source on the side of the main path with no branches or stores, so it runs through an empty corridor instead of crossing them.
- **Second entrance** into a node that already has an incoming edge: place the new source so it reaches that node from another side, usually directly below or above it.
- **Fan-out**: a side with k relationships needs at least `32 + 14 × (k − 1)`px (four need 74px). Spread a hub's counterparts over two or three sides, or enlarge the hub. Center a parent on its children and align a child with its only parent.

Before writing positions, trace each non-main relationship: its straight or one-bend corridor must not pass another node or cross another relationship. If it does, move the endpoint that is off the main path. # Repository-backed authoring

Use this reference when a diagram of any type must explain a real repository. The source is
the authority for responsibilities, calls, boundaries, and persistence. The
diagram is complete when the requested meaning is covered and every asserted
fact has supporting source evidence.

## Explore on demand

1. **Freeze identity.** From the target repository, record `git rev-parse
   HEAD`, `git remote get-url origin`, and `git status --short`. Remove HTTP(S)
   userinfo (including usernames, passwords, and tokens) before recording the
   origin or placing it in the candidate. Preserve its transport, port, path and
   `.git` suffix; do not rewrite an internal SSH origin as HTTPS. Pin the credential-free URL and
   forty-character revision in `meta.repository`. Use `link_mode: "local-only"`
   for an SSH origin, unsupported forge, intentionally local-only source links,
   or a local fixture whose HTTPS URL is only a repository identity; retain the
   URL and revision. Web links require a supported GitHub, Gitee, or GitLab HTTPS
   origin; GitHub, Gitee, gitlab.com, and a self-managed GitLab host declared with
   `provider: "gitlab"` match their SSH origin on the same host. If the
   worktree is dirty, note the changed paths in your reply; the candidate has no field for them. Repository evidence is verified
   against committed bytes at the pinned revision, not working-tree edits:
   inspect a clean checkout at that revision for any cited changed path. Do not
   present uncommitted bytes as evidence for `HEAD`; `local-only` does not record
   a verifiable snapshot of those bytes.

2. **Map the slice.** Use project instructions, manifests, entry points,
   registrations, and deployment configuration to locate candidate runtime
   units. Read the entry, configuration, and modules relevant to the request.
   Follow imports and call sites
   until the requested responsibility reaches its actual input, output, or
   side effect. Read a small connected slice instead of scanning the repository
   for a convenient label.

3. **Trace ownership.** Derive runtime and I/O relationships from the observed
   actor, operation, and target at their call sites; deployment and trust
   relationships use the corresponding configuration or enforcement evidence. Distinguish the controller requesting
   an operation from the runtime that executes it and the store receiving bytes.
   For a file or database edge, the source must identify its actual reader or
   writer; a responsibility statement such as “maintains tasks” does not prove
   direct I/O. Keep these facts with the source locations while reading, without
   a separate planning artifact. Choose which distinctions need separate
   nodes using [Composition and meaning](authoring-defaults.md#composition-and-meaning);
   discovering an implementation role does not automatically add it to the overview.
   A configured provider, an injected adapter, a local stub, and a durable
   service are different claims; label the one the source supports.

4. **Record evidence while reading.** Keep exact repository-relative paths and
   inclusive line ranges for each component and meaningful relationship. Follow
   actual branches, retries, fallbacks, and error handling. A function that is
   exported or configured but never called by the normal path is an optional
   capability, not a required runtime edge. For a claim about authoritative
   state change or control ownership, trace to the actual write or execution
   site and the conditions that permit it; an upstream caller alone does not
   establish those conditions.

5. **Name uncertainty.** Write unresolved questions beside the claim they
   affect: for example, “`writeFile` is called here; durability is unknown.”
   Resolve a question by reading the next relevant source range or preserve it
   as an explicit unknown. Never turn a label, package description, or config
   value into an unobserved service or behavior.

Stop exploring when every requested responsibility, relationship, and boundary
has supporting source entailment and the remaining unknowns cannot change that
coverage. There is no node, edge, citation, view, card, or boundary count to
hit. Do not add a summary step merely to signal completion.

Batch independent relevant files when known. Read source excerpts with their original
line numbers (for example, `nl -ba <file> | sed -n '40,90p'`). Copy citation
start and end lines from the displayed source, including the actual final line
when an excerpt reaches EOF. Each additional read should answer
an unresolved question that can change the diagram. Reuse concise facts and
their source ranges already verified in this task; across revisions, recheck
the affected entry points, configuration, dependencies, and evidence.

## Evidence by diagram type

Only the primary elements carry `sources`, at most three ranges each:
Architecture components, Workflow, Dataflow and Tree nodes, Sequence
participants, Lifecycle states, ERD entities, Class types, Timeline events and
Waterfall spans. Relationships, messages, flows and transitions have none: cite
the call, write or transition site on the element that owns it (the caller, the
writer, the state being left) and keep further evidence in a note or card. A
folder node cites its own README or entry file, or else the file that defines
or runs it. A Timeline event cites a file at the pinned revision that records
it, such as a changelog entry, and takes its time from a tag or commit in that
history, or noon local time for a date-only record. A tag or commit outside
that history is not citable. Say either in a card. A Waterfall without a
recorded trace uses `meta.evidence: "illustrative"` and keeps its durations
labelled as such; do not run the project only to time it.

## Choose an example by structure

Select the main example in the [Type router](../SKILL.md#type-router) before
loading its content, using the request and repository metadata already needed
for source inspection. Selection fits the existing read batch and needs no extra
message, command, or repository-wide scan. For mixed or unclear tasks, use the
requested responsibilities and entry points as they become known in normal
inspection; keep their actual roles. Read another example when a necessary
capability remains unexplained. Examples teach shape, not facts: a library need
not acquire filesystem nodes, and finished showcases still follow the
first-draft automatic-routing rule.

## Author from evidence

Use the mode's complete JSON shape, including repository identity,
components, and connections; every repository-backed component needs supporting source
references, while boundaries or cards are added only when they
answer a real reader question. Let automatic routes and automatic
viewBox sizing work first. Keep the primary path readable, put exception paths
beside their owner, and leave filesystem stores outside a control boundary when
the source shows a separate responsibility.

An existing example teaches field shape, not facts or arbitrary values. It does
not authorize a new boundary kind, a long note, a viewBox size, or a route
control. Consult the specific mode schema and `schemas/common.schema.json`
whether or not the selected example already contains the field; use the
schema's enum, length, identifier, and repository rules. Architecture
boundaries currently use `kind: "region"` or `kind: "security-group"`; source
references use `path`, `line`, and optional `end_line`.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/.claude/skills/alloq-implementation

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Pages use `admin_only=True`, but that only hides the page. Event handlers run over
the websocket for anyone with a session, so every handler protects itself.
`tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all states in the four
packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data** → `@rx.event` then `@requires_admin` (from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`). This is the default.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → `@requires_admin` is not
   allowed (it needs the state lock). Check admin inside `async with self` through
   `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` and list it in `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `ä`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

input.content:
# Database schema

[schema.html](schema.html) is an interactive entity-relationship diagram of every
table on `Base.metadata`: the alloq tables from `alloq_commons.entities` and the
login tables from `appkit_user`. Open it in a browser. It shows every column with
its PostgreSQL type, the keys, and one line per foreign key labelled with its
`ON DELETE` action.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `schema.erd.json` | Source of the diagram. Edit this file. |
| `schema.html` | Rendered diagram. Never edit by hand. |
| `schema.delivery.json` | Render receipt. It records the hashes of the JSON and the HTML. |

## Keeping it in sync

`tests/test_schema_doc.py` fails when the JSON and the SQLAlchemy models differ
(tables, columns, types, keys, foreign keys) or when the HTML was not rendered
from the current JSON. After a change to an entity or a migration:

1. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_schema_doc.py -q`. A failing column test prints
   the expected attributes of the table.
2. Update `schema.erd.json`. Place a new table in the grid (`row`, `col`) next to
   the tables of its domain (`tag`) and add a relationship for each new foreign
   key. Self-references cannot be drawn; mention them in the Conventions card.
3. Re-render with the archify skill (`/archify`), or run from the repo root:

   ```bash
   node ~/.claude/skills/archify/bin/archify.mjs finalize erd doc/database/schema.erd.json doc/database/schema.html --quality standard --out-dir /tmp/archify-schema --json
   ```

4. Run the test again and commit all three files.

Conventions in the JSON: types are PostgreSQL types, a trailing `null` marks a
nullable column, and the relationship `label` is the lowercase `ON DELETE` action.

# AGENTS.md

## 1) Golden Rules

1. **Think → Memory → Tools → Code → Memory.** Use code-reasoning; search Memory and claude-context first; minimal diff; write learnings back.
2. **Tests are truth.** Failures → fix code first. Change tests only if clearly wrong spec.
3. **Minimal diff.** Add tests before code. Keep simple.
4. **Consistency > cleverness.** Follow SOPs and stack idioms.
5. **Memory multiplies.** Persist decisions, patterns, error signatures, proven fixes.
6. **Files ≤ 1000 lines.** Exceed → refactor (see §5).
7. No extensive docs/summaries/comments unless requested.
8. No `--autogenerate` for Alembic migrations; write manually.
9. No `cat` to create files; use tools.
10. Log default: `logger.debug`. Important events: `logger.info`. Issues only: `logger.warning/error`. **No `print`.**

> Prefer *local* changes over cross-module refactors.

---

## 2) Task Bootstrap Pattern

```markdown
<!-- plan:start
goal: <one line clear goal>
constraints:
- Python 3.14; Reflex UI; FastAPI; SQLAlchemy 2.0; Alembic; Pydantic; appkit_mantine;
- logging: no f-strings in logger calls
- files ≤ 1000 lines; apply design patterns where appropriate
- minimal diff; add/adjust tests first
definition_of_done:
- tests pass; coverage ≥ 80% (non-Reflex classes & Reflex states); lint/type checks clean; memory updated
steps:
1) Search Memory for "<keywords>"
2) Draft/adjust failing test to capture expected behavior
3) Implement minimal code change
4) Run task test; iterate until green
5) Update Memory: decisions, patterns, error→fix
plan:end -->
```

---

## 3) Tooling Decision Matrix

| Situation | Primary | Secondary | Store to Memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API/pattern uncertainty | **Context7** | — | Canonical snippet + link; edge cases |
| Ecosystem bug/issue | **DuckDuckGo** | Context7 | Minimal repro; versions; workaround |
| Repeated test failure | **Memory (search)** | Context7 | Error signature → fix; root cause |
| New feature scaffold | **Context7** | — | How‑to snippet; checklist |
| House style/tooling | **This file** | Context7 | Checklist results |

Prefer official docs; widen via web search for cross-version issues.

---

## 4) SOP — Development Workflow

**Task Runner:** `task` (via `Taskfile.dist.yml`), not `make`.

### Prepare

1. Memory first — search prior solutions.
2. Reasoning plan — Task Bootstrap Pattern.
3. `task sync` (uv, Python 3.14).
4. `task test` — snapshot current failures.

### Triage Failures

- Read first failing assertion; map to spec.
- Tests match spec → fix code. Diverge → document; adjust spec/tests (after approval).
- Add/adjust unit tests to codify expected behavior.

### Implement (Minimal Diff)

- Tests-first for new behavior. Approved stacks only. Apply design patterns (see §5).
- **No `print`.** Use `logging` module.
- **No f-strings in logger calls:**

  ```python
  import logging

  log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  log.info("Loaded items: %d", count)  # ✅
  # log.info(f"Loaded items: {count}") # ❌
  ```

- After every code change, run `task lint` — not just at PR time.

### Quality Gates

- `task lint`, `task format`, `task typecheck`.
- `task test` — coverage ≥ **80%** non-Reflex classes & Reflex states.

### Learn → write to **Memory**

### Dependencies

- add dependencies always be using `uv add <library name>`

---

## 5) Python Code & Testing

Full rules in **python-coding** skill. Key:

- Python 3.14; uv; line length **88**.
- No f-strings in logger calls.
- Files **≤ 1000 lines**.
- Test coverage ≥ 80%.
- Type annotations on **all** functions/methods.

---

## 6) Security & Config

- No credentials in code/history; `.env` local, Key Vault prod.
- Non-secret YAML; env `__` override pattern.
- Parameterized logs; no sensitive values.
- `SecretStr` → `.get_secret_value()`.
- Update vulnerable deps; document CVE-driven updates in commits & Memory.

---

## 7) Search SOPs

- **Context7 first** for framework truths; cite in Memory.
- **DuckDuckGo** for cross-version issues; prefer official docs.
- Store only final answer: minimal snippet + rationale + version pins + link.

---

## 8) Task Checklist / Definition of Done

- [ ] Tests added/updated; all green
- [ ] Coverage ≥ 80%
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck` pass
- [ ] No file > 1000 lines
- [ ] Clean architecture, no code smells, used python-clean-code principles
- [ ] Migrations reviewed & documented
- [ ] Documentation & README.md updated
- [ ] Memory updated (decisions, patterns, error→fix, learnings)

---

## 9) Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `python-coding` | Python 3.14 style, logging, type annotations, design patterns, testing |
| `python-clean-code` | Enforce Clean Code Developer (CCD) architecture and software quality principles |
| `code-cleanup` | Refactor and simplify Python files modified in the current session if they get complex/big |
| `boost` | Use when the user wants to refine, sharpen, or expand a rough idea into a detailed implementation prompt |
| `reflex-state-and-architecture` | State design, event handlers, background tasks, form validation, page factory, service registry, repo pattern, DB models, architecture |
| `reflex-testing-state` | Pytest unit tests for Reflex State — event handlers, computed vars, substates |
| `reflex-docs` | Reflex.dev framework documentation |
| `frontend-design` | Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces |
| `appkit-mantine-reference` | Full API for appkit_mantine components — inputs, layout, overlays, charts, data display, navigation |
| `appkit-commons` | app configuration, service registry, DB repository pattern, DB entities, DB custom column types, scheduler |

# Database schema

[schema.html](schema.html) is an interactive entity-relationship diagram of every
table on `Base.metadata`: the alloq tables from `alloq_commons.entities` and the
login tables from `appkit_user`. Open it in a browser. It shows every column with
its PostgreSQL type, the keys, and one line per foreign key labelled with its
`ON DELETE` action.

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `schema.erd.json` | Source of the diagram. Edit this file. |
| `schema.html` | Rendered diagram. Never edit by hand. |
| `schema.delivery.json` | Render receipt. It records the hashes of the JSON and the HTML. |

## Keeping it in sync

`tests/test_schema_doc.py` fails when the JSON and the SQLAlchemy models differ
(tables, columns, types, keys, foreign keys) or when the HTML was not rendered
from the current JSON. After a change to an entity or a migration:

1. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_schema_doc.py -q`. A failing column test prints
   the expected attributes of the table.
2. Update `schema.erd.json`. Place a new table in the grid (`row`, `col`) next to
   the tables of its domain (`tag`) and add a relationship for each new foreign
   key. Self-references cannot be drawn; mention them in the Conventions card.
3. Re-render with the archify skill (`/archify`), or run from the repo root:

   ```bash
   node ~/.claude/skills/archify/bin/archify.mjs finalize erd doc/database/schema.erd.json doc/database/schema.html --quality standard --out-dir /tmp/archify-schema --json
   ```

4. Run the test again and commit all three files.

Conventions in the JSON: types are PostgreSQL types, a trailing `null` marks a
nullable column, and the relationship `label` is the lowercase `ON DELETE` action.

I've created the [database schema ERD](</Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/doc/database/schema.html>), an interactive page you open in a browser. It covers all 20 tables, both the alloq ones and the appkit_user login tables. Each column shows its PostgreSQL type and its keys. Each foreign key is drawn as a line labelled with its `ON DELETE` action. The tables are grouped by domain: projects, staffing, people, auth login, auth password and calendar. I put it in the existing `doc/` folder, since the repo has no `docs/`. Automated checks passed, and I looked at one screenshot at 1440px.

**How it stays in sync**
- **Source file:** [schema.erd.json](doc/database/schema.erd.json) is what you edit. `schema.html` is rendered from it, and `schema.delivery.json` records the hashes of both.
- **Test:** [test_schema_doc.py](tests/test_schema_doc.py) compares the JSON with `Base.metadata`: tables, columns, types, keys, and foreign keys with their `ON DELETE` actions. When a table differs, the test prints the columns it expects. It also fails if the HTML was not re-rendered after the JSON changed.
- **Rule:** I added a checklist line to [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (which `CLAUDE.md` points to) and to the alloq-implementation skill. The steps to update and re-render are in [doc/database/README.md](doc/database/README.md).
- **Limit:** the diagram tool can't draw a table pointing to itself, so `employees.manager_id` is described in a note on the diagram instead. The test skips it.

**One schema problem I found:** `auth_password_history`, `auth_password_reset_tokens` and `auth_password_reset_requests` are defined in appkit_user, but no migration creates them and nothing else does either. So a database built from the migrations is missing these three tables. The diagram flags this, and I opened a separate task card to write the migration.

**Test results:** the new tests pass and coverage is 89%. One existing test fails: `test_known_revisions_are_the_alembic_history`. The cause is your uncommitted booking-number migration (`ef56ab78cd90`), which isn't in `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py` yet. My changes didn't cause it. Nothing is committed.
